q: A team member wants to paste confidential customer data into a public generative AI tool to summarize requirements. What should the project manager do?
o: Stop this and follow organizational data-protection and AI-use policies, using approved tools
Allow it because it saves time
Allow it if the data is deleted afterward
Ask the customer after the data has been uploaded
e: Responsible AI use requires protecting confidential and personal data, complying with policies and regulations, and using approved tools. Convenience does not justify a data-protection breach.

q: An AI scheduling assistant recommends a plan that consistently assigns fewer development opportunities to certain team members. What concern should the project manager address?
o: Potential bias in the AI model or its training data
The plan's critical path length
The tool's license cost
The number of activities in the schedule
e: AI models can reproduce or amplify bias present in historical data. Project managers should monitor AI outputs for fairness and maintain accountability for people-related decisions.

q: Which statement BEST describes accountability when AI tools are used in a project?
o: Humans remain accountable for decisions informed by AI outputs
The AI vendor is accountable for all project decisions
No one is accountable because decisions are automated
The PMO is accountable for every AI recommendation
e: AI augments human capability, but accountability for project decisions remains with people, consistent with the 'be an accountable leader' principle.

q: The organization wants to adopt AI tools across its projects. What should the project manager do to support this change?
o: Plan training, set usage guidelines and pilot the tools before wider rollout
Mandate immediate use on all projects without guidance
Ban AI tools entirely
Let each team member decide independently with no guidelines
e: Introducing AI is an organizational change: piloting, training, governance guidelines and feedback loops support effective and responsible adoption.

q: Which three dimensions are commonly considered under the sustainability principle?
o: Environmental, social and economic
Scope, schedule and cost
People, process and business environment
Plan, do and check
e: Sustainability considers environmental, social and economic impacts (sometimes called the triple bottom line) across the project and the life of its outputs.

q: A construction project manager selects suppliers that use recycled materials and lower-emission transport, even though the cost is slightly higher. What principle does this reflect?
o: Integrate sustainability within all project areas
Focus on value only in financial terms
Embed quality into processes and deliverables
Build an empowered culture
e: Integrating sustainability into sourcing decisions considers environmental impact alongside cost, supporting long-term value.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of social sustainability in a project?
o: Hiring and training local workers and ensuring fair working conditions
Reducing the project's energy consumption
Negotiating lower prices with suppliers
Reducing documentation
e: Social sustainability concerns people and communities: fair labor practices, health and safety, community engagement, inclusion and local capability building.

q: A sponsor asks why sustainability metrics should be tracked when the project's financial targets are met. What is the BEST response?
o: Sustainability affects long-term value, regulatory compliance and reputation
Sustainability is only relevant for environmental projects
Sustainability metrics are required only at project closure
Sustainability replaces financial targets
e: Sustainability considerations support long-term value creation, meet stakeholder and regulatory expectations (e.g., ESG reporting), and reduce reputational and operational risk.

q: New ESG reporting regulations require the organization to disclose project emissions. What should the project manager do?
o: Identify the data needed, assign responsibility and integrate measurement into project controls
Wait for the regulation to be enforced
Estimate emissions at the end of the project
Exclude emissions data because it is not part of scope
e: Planning compliance with new external requirements means integrating them into plans, data collection and reporting, with clear ownership.

q: A project team holds a bidder conference before proposals are submitted. What is the PRIMARY purpose?
o: To ensure all prospective sellers have the same understanding of the procurement
To select the winning seller
To negotiate final prices
To inspect the seller's facilities
e: Bidder conferences give all prospective sellers a clear, common understanding of the requirements, ensuring fairness and better proposals.

q: During contract execution, the seller is consistently late with deliverables. What should the project manager do FIRST?
o: Review performance against the contract terms and discuss corrective action with the seller
Terminate the contract immediately
Withhold all payments without notice
Ignore the delays as long as quality is acceptable
e: Contract administration involves monitoring seller performance against the agreement and working with the seller to correct issues, using contractual remedies if needed.

q: Which of the following must happen before a procurement can be formally closed?
o: All deliverables accepted and contractual obligations, including payments and claims, settled
The project's final report is published
The vendor delivers a lessons-learned presentation
The sponsor signs the project charter again
e: Procurement closure requires confirming that all work is complete and accepted, open claims are resolved, final payments are made and records are archived.

q: Which fixed-price contract type includes a provision to adjust the price for changes in conditions such as inflation over a multi-year period?
o: Fixed price with economic price adjustment (FP-EPA)
Firm fixed price
Fixed price incentive fee
Cost plus fixed fee
e: FP-EPA contracts allow pre-defined final price adjustments for changing conditions (e.g., inflation, commodity prices), which is useful for long-term contracts.

q: A PMO wants to improve how lessons are shared across projects. Which initiative BEST supports this goal?
o: Communities of practice and an accessible knowledge repository
Mandatory 50-page lessons-learned reports
A policy that only project managers can access lessons
Removing retrospectives to save time
e: PMOs can foster knowledge transfer through communities of practice, accessible repositories and facilitated sharing sessions, supporting continuous improvement across the organization.

q: An organization outsources a module to a vendor using a hybrid approach. Which practice MOST improves collaboration and outcomes?
o: Include the vendor's team in joint planning, reviews and shared definitions of done
Communicate only through formal contract letters
Keep the vendor's team separate until final delivery
Require the vendor to use a different methodology
e: Collaborative relationships with sellers, especially in adaptive or hybrid work, rely on shared ceremonies, transparency and common quality criteria rather than only arm's-length contract management.
